slo_title: Describe multiple-processor scheduling and its challenges

mcq.q: Which Pthread scope setting allows user-level threads to compete within the same process ?
What is the main difference between coarse-grained and fine-grained multithreading ?

options.B: Fine-grained allows simultaneous execution of all threads
options.D: Coarse-grained runs only one thread at a time

mcq.q: Which of the following best describes the concept of Processor Affinity ?

options.A: A process always runs on a different processor every time
options.B: A process runs on the slowest available processor
options.C: A process prefers to run on the same processor to benefit from cache memory
options.D: A process only runs on processors with more threads

mcq.answer_text: A process prefers to run on the same processor to benefit from cache memory

mcq.q: In Symmetric Multiprocessing , what is true about the processors?

options.A: Only the master processor schedules tasks
options.B: Each processor uses a different operating system
options.C: All processors share scheduling responsibilities equally
options.D: Only user processes are executed by the processors

mcq.answer_text: All processors share scheduling responsibilities equally

mcq.q: Push migration in load balancing refers to:

options.B: Periodic checking and redistributing load among processors

mcq.answer_text: Periodic checking and redistributing load among processors

sq.q: Differentiate between Symmetric and Asymmetric Multiprocessing with two points each.
answer: Symmetric : All processors self-scheduling; duplicates of OS; system continues if one fails (50%)
Symmetric : All processors self-scheduling; duplicates of OS; system continues if one fails (50%)
Asymmetric : One processor (master) handles all I/O and scheduling; reduces data sharing (50%)

sq.q: Explain the two types of contention scope in thread scheduling with examples.
answer: PCS (Process-Contention Scope): User-level threads compete within a process (50%)
PCS (Process-Contention Scope): User-level threads compete within a process (50%)
SCS (System-Contention Scope): Kernel-level threads compete across system (50%)
SCS (System-Contention Scope): Kernel-level threads compete across system (50%)
